newsitem.title: UK: Zinc stars on LME, ends near new 6-3/4 year high.
newsitem.headline: Zinc stars on LME, ends near new 6-3/4 year high.

text.p: Zinc prices charged higher once more during Tuesday LME trading, clocking up yet another 6-3/4 year high as technical tightness developed in the autumn months, traders said.
Elsewhere on the base metals complex the trends were mixed, with copper and tin sagging, but aluminium, nickel and lead in the plus column.

In zinc, speculative buying was sucked in to a market that is tightening all the time. Cash/threes contracted into just $2/3 contango at one stage, with a hefty backwardation developing from the September date.
"It does look as though it (tightness) is building up later in the year," Angus MacMillan of LME trader Billiton Metals said.
This, and the influx of fund buying, is tending to offset an expected slowdown that should take place in the current third quarter, he said.
Traders said the market continues to be underpinned by talk of major Far Eastern shorts battling against influential European merchants. Last trade was at $1,437, up $19.
Billiton's MacMillan noted that there was resistance around $1,450, which the market was backing off from. "We may now see a correction," he said.
Copper fluctuated throughout the session, as nervousness built up ahead of the crucial July traded option declarations on Wednesday.
Spread rates also fluctuated, but there was enough borrowing of various July dates to keep the tightness bubbling along. Cash/threes was at a $122/132 backwardation at the close.

Last business was at $2,393, down $29 from Monday. Once the options and the uncertainties associated with delat-hedging are out of the way, the market has the potential to strike higher again, traders said.

Aluminium held onto the bridgehead above the $1,600 level, although there was plenty of overhead resistance and some producer-linked selling to prevent a significant advance. Prices finished at $1,603, up $5 from yesterday.
Nickel price movements were whippier during the afternoon, with the market scrapping its way to a higher close of $6,930, up $70.

Traders said the positive impetus of lost output at Outokumpu's smelter in Finland tended to offset news Norilsk gas supplies were back to normal. Also, the market had become oversold on Friday and Monday.
The lead market gained from the strength of zinc, as well as some July/August borrowing, and prices climbed above $630. Three months ended at $636, up $9.
Tin, however, was depressed by quiet physicals and some softening in premiums, which resulted in some tired long liquidation. Three months ended at $5,530, down $40.
A quiet alloy market finished at a stable $1,450/55 a tonne.
